1.shloka:
सकृच्छ्रवणमात्रेण ब्रह्मज्ञानं यतो भवेत् ।
ब्रह्मज्ञानावलीमाला सर्वेषां मोक्षसिद्धये ॥ १॥
1.transliteration:
sakṛcchravaṇamātreṇa brahmajñānaṃ yato bhavet .
brahmajñānāvalīmālā sarveṣāṃ mokṣasiddhaye .. 1..
1.translation: The work entitled Brahma Jnānavali Māla, by hearing which just once knowledge of Brahman is attained, enables all to attain liberation.

2.translation: Unattached am I, unattached am I, ever free from attachment of any kind; I am of the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and ever unchanging.

3.translation: I am eternal, I am pure (free from the control of Maya). I am ever liberated. I am formless, indestructible and changeless. I am of the nature of infinite bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

4.translation: I am eternal, I am free from blemish, I am formless, I am indestructible and changeless. I am of the nature of supreme bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

5.translation: I am pure consciousness, I revel in my own Self. I am of the nature of indivisible (concentrated) bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

6.translation: I am the indwelling consciousness, I am calm (free from all agitation), I am beyond prakrti (Maya), I am of the nature of eternal bliss, I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

7.shloka:
तत्त्वातीतः परात्माहं मध्यातीतः परः शिवः ।
मायातीतः परंज्योतिरहमेवाहमव्ययः ॥ ७॥
7.transliteration:
tattvātītaḥ parātmāhaṃ madhyātītaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ .
māyātītaḥ paraṃjyotirahamevāhamavyayaḥ .. 7..
7.translation: I am the supreme Self, beyond all the categories (such as prakrti, mahat, ahankara, etc.,), I am the supreme auspicious One, beyond all those in the middle. I am beyond maya. I am the supreme light. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

8.translation: I am beyond all the different forms. I am of the nature of pure consciousness. I am never subject to decline. I am of the nature of bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

9.translation: There is neither maya nor its effects such as the body for me. I am of the same nature and self-luminous. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

10.translation: I am beyond the three gunas-sattva, rajas, and tamas. I am the witness of even Brahma and others. I am of the nature of infinite bliss. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

11.translation: I am the inner controller, I am immutable, I am all-pervading. I am myself the supreme Self. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

12.translation: I am devoid of parts. I am actionless. I am the self of all. I am the primordial one. I am the ancient, eternal one. I am the directly intuited self. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

13.translation: I am the witness of all pairs of opposites. I am immovable. I am eternal. I am the witness of everything. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

14.shloka:
प्रज्ञानघन एवाहं विज्ञानघन एव च ।
अकर्ताहमभोक्ताहमहमेवाहमव्ययः ॥ १४॥
14.transliteration:
prajñānaghana evāhaṃ vijñānaghana eva ca .
akartāhamabhoktāhamahamevāhamavyayaḥ .. 14..
14.translation: I am a mass of awareness and of consciousness. I am not a doer nor an experiencer. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

15.translation: I am without any support, and I am the support of all. I have no desires to be fulfilled. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

16.translation: I am free from the three kinds of afflictions- those in the body, those from other beings and those caused by higher powers. I am different from the gross, subtle and causal bodies. I am the witness of the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep. I am the very Self, indestructible and changeless.

17.shloka:
दृग्दृश्यौ द्वौ पदार्थौ स्तः परस्परविलक्षणौ ।
दृग्ब्रह्म दृश्यं मायेति सर्ववेदान्तडिण्डिमः ॥ १७॥
17.transliteration:
dṛgdṛśyau dvau padārthau staḥ parasparavilakṣaṇau .
dṛgbrahma dṛśyaṃ māyeti sarvavedāntaḍiṇḍimaḥ .. 17..
17.translation: There are two things which are different from each other. They are the seer and the seen. The seer is Brahman and the seen is Maya. This is what all Vedanta proclaims.

18.shloka:
अहं साक्षीति यो विद्याद्विविच्यैवं पुनः पुनः ।
स एव मुक्तः सो विद्वानिति वेदान्तडिण्डिमः ॥ १८॥
18.transliteration:
ahaṃ sākṣīti yo vidyādvivicyaivaṃ punaḥ punaḥ .
sa eva muktaḥ so vidvāniti vedāntaḍiṇḍimaḥ .. 18..
18.translation: He who realizes after repeated contemplation that he is a mere witness, he alone is liberated. He is the enlightened one. This is proclaimed by Vedanta

19.shloka:
घटकुड्यादिकं सर्वं मृत्तिकामात्रमेव च ।
तद्वद्ब्रह्म जगत्सर्वमिति वेदान्तडिण्डिमः ॥ १९॥
19.transliteration:
ghaṭakuḍyādikaṃ sarvaṃ mṛttikāmātrameva ca .
tadvadbrahma jagatsarvamiti vedāntaḍiṇḍimaḥ .. 19..
19.translation: The pot, wall, etc., are all nothing but clay. Likewise, the entire universe is nothing but Brahman. This is proclaimed by Vedanta.

20.shloka:
ब्रह्म सत्यं जगन्मिथ्या जीवो ब्रह्मैव नापरः ।
अनेन वेद्यं सच्छास्त्रमिति वेदान्तडिण्डिमः ॥ २०॥
20.transliteration:
brahma satyaṃ jaganmithyā jīvo brahmaiva nāparaḥ .
anena vedyaṃ sacchāstramiti vedāntaḍiṇḍimaḥ .. 20..
20.translation: Brahman is real, the universe is mithya (it cannot be categorized as either real or unreal). The jiva is Brahman itself and not different. This should be understood as the correct Sastra. This is proclaimed by Vedanta.

21.shloka:
अन्तर्ज्योतिर्बहिर्ज्योतिः प्रत्यग्ज्योतिः परात्परः ।
ज्योतिर्ज्योतिः स्वयंज्योतिरात्मज्योतिः शिवोऽस्म्यहम् ॥ २१॥
21.transliteration:
antarjyotirbahirjyotiḥ pratyagjyotiḥ parātparaḥ .
jyotirjyotiḥ svayaṃjyotirātmajyotiḥ śivo'smyaham .. 21..
21.translation: I am the auspicious one, the inner light and the outer light, the indwelling light, higher than the highest, the light of all lights, self-luminous, the light that is the Self.
